newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WHEAT HARVESTING TO END BY AUG 15 - MINISTRY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WHEAT HARVESTING TO END BY AUG 15 - MINISTRY.

text.p: Hungary has completed most of its wheat harvesting and the remainder should be finished by about August 15, an Agriculture Ministry Official said on Thursday.
"About 80 percent of the harvesting is done and if the weather holds, it will be all but finished by August 15," Sandor Oravecz told Reuters.
He added that only some small areas in north Hungary would have unharvested wheat by that time.
Hungary expects a five million tonnes wheat crop this year, up from 3.9 million tonnes in 1996.
Persistent rains, however, have lowered the quality of the wheat crop but producers, traders and ministry officials had different opinions on the extent of the damage.
"When producers store their wheat harvest without giving samples, it is difficult to assess the damage," said Sandor Oravecz, but confirmed there was some quality damage.
"The quality has worsened, but not to the extent some people say it did".

Janos Csuka of Concordia Public Storage said that on the south Hungarian plains some 50 percent of the wheat was up to Hungarian milling standards but that in the western region of Transdanubia that ratio was around 10 percent.
Traders said earlier that they expected a 40-60 milling wheat to feed wheat ratio this year compared with the customary 60-40 ratio.

Csuka also said that while wheat quality in Hungary was traditionally assessed by gluten content, the starch-to-sugar gradient, an important west European benchmark which shows sings of incipient germination, was also bad in many parts of Hungary.
